title: Request panes
brief: Scripts tab (pre-request and test editors, empty state that invites a first script), Settings tab (timeout, follow redirects, verify TLS as visible controls with a default state), Params/Headers grid with readable column divisions, and a draggable split between the request and the response with a visible handle, resize cursor and collapsed and expanded states. Built on the Bolt shell of design/bolt-v2/01-main.html; every editable value reads as editable.

artboards.title: Stacked split with a grip
artboards.tradeoff: Closest to today's layout: a 9 px gutter with a dotted grip between request and response, spreadsheet grid with a line on every side, both scripts stacked, settings as Default / On / Off segments; the two stacked editors get short when the response is open

artboards.title: Side by side
artboards.tradeoff: Request and response next to each other (the Split button turns it on) with a column handle and a 40 px collapsed column; editing and reading the response at once, but each side gets about 550 px: the grid drops its description column and one script shows at a time

artboards.title: Response header as the handle
artboards.tradeoff: DBFlux results-panel pattern: the whole response header row drags, with Collapse / Split / Maximize presets; request sections move to a vertical list so the DBFlux data grid, side-by-side scripts and an explicit override table fit; costs 140 px of width and changes where the request tabs live
